concepts.description: Explores the behavior of functions as input approaches a certain value, forming the foundational understanding of continuity and the basis for calculus.
concepts.name: Limits and Continuity

concepts.description: Introduces the concept of instantaneous rate of change and slope of a tangent line, along with systematic rules for computing derivatives of various functions.
concepts.name: Derivatives and Rules of Differentiation

concepts.description: Establishes the crucial connection between differentiation and integration, providing a method for evaluating definite integrals using antiderivatives.
concepts.name: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus

concepts.description: Covers various methods for finding antiderivatives and evaluating integrals, including substitution, integration by parts, trigonometric substitution, and partial fractions.
concepts.name: Techniques of Integration

concepts.description: Utilizes definite integrals to calculate areas between curves and volumes of solids of revolution using methods like disk, washer, and shell.
concepts.name: Applications of Integration to Area and Volume

concepts.description: Applies derivatives to analyze the properties of functions, such as intervals of increase/decrease, concavity, and local extrema, to accurately sketch their graphs.
concepts.name: Curve Sketching

concepts.description: Uses calculus to find the maximum or minimum values of a function, often applied to solve real-world problems involving quantities like area, volume, or cost.
concepts.name: Optimization

concepts.description: Involves finding the rate at which one quantity is changing based on the known rates of other related quantities, often in dynamic physical scenarios.
concepts.name: Related Rates

concepts.description: A technique for differentiating functions that are not explicitly defined in terms of one variable, often used for equations involving mixed variables.
concepts.name: Implicit Differentiation

concepts.description: States that for a continuous and differentiable function on a closed interval, there is at least one point where the instantaneous rate of change equals the average rate of change.
concepts.name: Mean Value Theorem

concepts.description: A method used to evaluate indeterminate forms of limits by taking the derivatives of the numerator and denominator.
concepts.name: L'Hopital's Rule

concepts.description: Approximates the area under a curve by dividing it into a series of rectangles, leading to the formal definition of the definite integral.
concepts.name: Riemann Sums

concepts.description: Introduces simple differential equations and methods for solving them, providing a foundation for understanding models of change.
concepts.name: Differential Equations Basics

concepts.description: Explores ordered lists of numbers and the sums of these lists, including concepts like convergence and divergence, which are typically covered at the end of Calculus I or in Calculus II.
concepts.name: Sequences and Series
